Do not submit a hand-composed grid.
3. Run the transform on every received input/output pair and compare complete grids exactly. Preserve demos as received; never use a sparse reconstruction or hand-derived expected output, since transcription errors can masquerade as rule failures. After each code edit, rerun every pair; an exception or mismatch means the program is not validated, so do not submit yet. Before submission, check that the returned grid has 1–30 nonempty rows of equal length, with only integer cell values 0–9; output dimensions need not equal the input dimensions. Once all pairs match and the test result passes these checks, submit only that returned grid. Treat the action JSON as the puzzle's response protocol, not a tool invocation: each puzzle reply must end with exactly one action object; request demos by replying with `{"action":"request_demos"}`, and submit only with a program-produced grid.
